result:
Fixed in `anthrouter/pace.py`. The 30 tests in `tests/test_pace.py` pass. I didn't wait for the full suite — it timed out in the foreground and is still running in the background.

The bug was in `period_workday_dates`. `period_end` is the exclusive first instant of the next month, but the code counted its local date inclusively. In UTC that pulled in Oct 1, 2026 (a Thursday), so September got 23 workdays instead of 22. The same overcount happens in any timezone at or east of UTC.

The end date is now taken from the period's last instant (`period_end - 1µs`). I updated the docstring to match.
